meta.schoolContext: Conestoga College pre-assessment biology appears to be a short, multiple-choice placement-style test focused on foundational high school biology concepts. The sample questions emphasize factual recall, basic vocabulary, and simple understanding of human anatomy, cells, and biomolecules rather than application or lab-based reasoning.

questions.text: Blood flows directly from the right ventricle in the human heart to the:
questions.explanation: The right ventricle pumps deoxygenated blood to the lungs through the pulmonary arteries.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Blood does not flow directly from the right ventricle to the left atrium.
wrongAnswerHints.1: The ventricles are not directly connected.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Blood enters the right ventricle from the right atrium, not the reverse.

questions.text: Genes are located in (on) the:
questions.explanation: Genes are segments of DNA located on chromosomes.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Centrioles assist in cell division but do not contain genes.
wrongAnswerHints.1: Mitochondria contain some DNA but genes are primarily located on chromosomes.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The endoplasmic reticulum helps synthesize proteins and lipids.

questions.text: A constant body temperature is characteristic of:
questions.explanation: Mammals and birds are endothermic animals that regulate their body temperature internally.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Reptiles are ectothermic and rely on environmental heat.
wrongAnswerHints.1: Birds maintain body temperature, reptiles do not.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Birds also maintain a constant body temperature.

questions.text: The basic functional unit of the nervous system is the:
questions.explanation: The neuron is the fundamental cell responsible for transmitting nerve impulses.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The spinal cord is composed of many neurons.
wrongAnswerHints.2: A nerve is a bundle of neuron fibers.
wrongAnswerHints.3: A dendrite is only one part of a neuron.

questions.text: The pH of blood is slightly basic. Which of the following would be most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Human blood normally has a pH of approximately 7.35–7.45.

wrongAnswerHints.1: 4.6 is strongly acidic.
wrongAnswerHints.3: 13.8 is extremely basic and incompatible with life.

questions.text: Which aspect of a protein determines whether it will function as an enzyme?
questions.explanation: An enzyme’s function depends on its 3D shape, especially the shape of its active site. The question’s options are awkward, but “interior” is the best match because the enzyme’s internal folding and active-site arrangement determine what it can bind and catalyze.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The surface alone does not determine enzyme specificity; the functional active site depends on overall protein folding.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Weight does not determine whether a protein acts as an enzyme.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Colour has no role in enzyme function.

questions.text: Granules which are the sites of protein synthesis within a cell are:
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis in the cell. They read messenger RNA and assemble amino acids into polypeptides.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis, not protein synthesis.
wrongAnswerHints.1: Mitochondria are mainly responsible for cellular respiration and ATP production.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The endoplasmic reticulum can help with protein processing, but ribosomes are the actual protein-synthesizing granules.

questions.text: Organelles associated with cellular respiration are called:
questions.explanation: Mitochondria are the organelles where most cellular respiration occurs in eukaryotic cells. They convert energy from food molecules into ATP, the cell’s usable energy currency.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins, but it does not perform cellular respiration.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis in plant cells, not cellular respiration.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Lysosomes digest and recycle materials, but they are not the main site of respiration.

topics: Cell membrane transport and selective permeability

questions.text: The ability of cell membrane to allow certain substances to enter or leave the cell is called:
questions.explanation: Selective permeability is the property of the cell membrane that allows some substances to pass through while blocking others. This control helps the cell maintain a stable internal environment.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Diffusion is the movement of particles from high to low concentration, not the membrane property itself.
wrongAnswerHints.1: This is not a standard biology term for membrane transport.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Osmosis is the diffusion of water specifically, not the general membrane property.

questions.text: The most common method of cell division in the body is called:
questions.explanation: Mitosis is the most common type of cell division in the body because it produces two genetically identical daughter cells for growth and repair. It occurs in somatic cells throughout the body.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Osmosis is movement of water across a membrane, not cell division.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Meiosis makes sex cells (gametes), not most body cells.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Halitosis means bad breath, so it is unrelated to cell division.

topics: Biological scale and levels of organization

questions.text: A nerve cell is smaller than a(n):
questions.explanation: A neuron is a cell, and cells are smaller than tissues. Tissues are made of groups of similar cells working together, so they are a higher level of organization than a single nerve cell.

wrongAnswerHints.0: A virus is generally smaller than a cell, so a neuron is not smaller than a virus.
wrongAnswerHints.1: An atom is much smaller than a cell, so this cannot be correct.
wrongAnswerHints.2: A proton is smaller than an atom and far smaller than a cell.

topics: Human circulatory system and heart anatomy

questions.text: A person standing facing you has his heart located:
questions.explanation: The heart is located in the chest, above the stomach. In anatomical terms, it lies superior to the stomach and within the thoracic cavity.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The heart is not above the brain; it is in the chest.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The heart is in front of the spinal cord, not behind it.
wrongAnswerHints.3: The heart is not below the ovary; the ovary is in the pelvic region.

questions.text: The cell nucleus is located:
options: next to the protons and neutrons
questions.explanation: The nucleus is a membrane-bound organelle found in the cytoplasm of eukaryotic cells. It contains the cell’s DNA and helps control cell activities.

wrongAnswerHints.0: The nucleus is not outside the cell membrane; it is inside the cell.
wrongAnswerHints.1: Mitochondria are separate organelles and do not contain the nucleus.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Protons and neutrons are found in atoms, not inside cells.

topics: Biological scale and levels of organization

questions.text: Which of the following is the highest level of complexity in the human body?
questions.explanation: Among the choices, an organ is the highest level of complexity. Organs are made of multiple tissues working together, while tissues are made of cells and cells are made of molecules.

wrongAnswerHints.0: A molecule is smaller and less complex than a cell or tissue.
wrongAnswerHints.1: A cell is a basic unit of life, but it is less complex than an organ.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Tissue is made of similar cells, so it is below the level of organ.

topics: Human circulatory system and heart anatomy

questions.text: Your blood flows throughout your body because of a(n):
questions.explanation: Blood flows because of pressure differences created by the heart pumping blood through vessels. Blood moves from areas of higher pressure to lower pressure, which drives circulation.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Temperature differences do not directly drive blood flow through the body.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Concentration gradients help move some substances, but they are not the main force moving blood.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Electrical gradients are important in nerve and muscle activity, not the main cause of blood flow.

topics: Human circulatory system and heart anatomy

questions.text: Which chamber of the human heart pumps oxygen-rich blood to the body through the aorta?
questions.explanation: The left ventricle is the main pumping chamber that sends oxygenated blood into the aorta for distribution to the body.

wrongAnswerHints.0: The right atrium receives deoxygenated blood from the body.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The right ventricle pumps blood to the lungs, not to the body.
wrongAnswerHints.3: The left atrium receives oxygenated blood from the lungs.

questions.text: A gene is best described as a segment of DNA located on a:
questions.explanation: Genes are sections of DNA found on chromosomes.

wrongAnswerHints.1: Ribosomes make proteins, but they do not contain genes.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Lysosomes contain digestive enzymes, not genes.

questions.text: Which type of organism is an endotherm?
questions.explanation: Endotherms regulate body temperature mainly by generating internal heat. Humans are endotherms.

wrongAnswerHints.1: Frogs are ectotherms and depend on environmental heat.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Snakes are ectotherms.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Fish are ectotherms.

questions.text: Which cell part is the main site of protein synthesis?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the structures where proteins are assembled.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The nucleus contains DNA and controls cell activities.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Vacuoles mainly store water and other materials.
wrongAnswerHints.3: The Golgi apparatus packages and modifies proteins after they are made.

questions.text: What is the normal pH range of human blood?
questions.explanation: Human blood is slightly basic, with a normal pH of about 7.4.

wrongAnswerHints.1: A pH of 2.0 is strongly acidic and far too low for blood.
wrongAnswerHints.2: A pH of 9.5 is too basic for normal blood.
wrongAnswerHints.3: A pH of 5.0 is acidic and not normal for blood.

topics: Human circulatory system and heart anatomy

questions.text: Which chamber of the heart receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs before it is pumped to the rest of the body?
questions.explanation: The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins.

wrongAnswerHints.0: This chamber receives oxygen-poor blood from the body.
wrongAnswerHints.2: This chamber pumps blood to the lungs.
wrongAnswerHints.3: This chamber pumps blood out to the body, but it does not receive blood from the lungs first.

questions.text: A gene is a segment of DNA found on a(n):
questions.explanation: Genes are segments of DNA located on chromosomes.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Ribosomes help make proteins, but they do not carry genes.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Vacuoles store materials in the cell.
wrongAnswerHints.3: The cell membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

questions.text: Sweating helps the human body cool down. This is an example of:
questions.explanation: Thermoregulation is the process of maintaining a stable internal body temperature.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Digestion is the breakdown of food.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Photosynthesis occurs in plants, not in human temperature control.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Fertilization is the joining of sex cells.

questions.text: Which part of a neuron usually carries impulses away from the cell body?
questions.explanation: The axon carries nerve impulses away from the cell body.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The nucleus controls the cell, but it does not carry impulses.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Animal cells do not have cell walls.
wrongAnswerHints.3: A synapse is the gap between neurons where signals are passed.

questions.text: Which pH value would best represent a strongly acidic substance?
questions.explanation: A pH of 2 is strongly acidic because it is far below 7.

wrongAnswerHints.1: A pH of 7 is neutral.
wrongAnswerHints.2: A pH above 7 is basic.
wrongAnswerHints.3: A pH of 10 is basic, not acidic.

questions.text: During cell division, chromosomes are duplicated so that each new cell receives a complete set of genetic material. Where are chromosomes found in a human cell?
questions.explanation: Chromosomes are located in the nucleus of a human cell.

wrongAnswerHints.0: The cytoplasm contains many cell structures, but not chromosomes.
wrongAnswerHints.1: The cell membrane surrounds the cell.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Ribosomes build proteins.

questions.text: Which body process helps mammals keep a stable internal temperature when the environment gets cold?
questions.explanation: Shivering produces heat and helps maintain body temperature in endotherms such as mammals.

wrongAnswerHints.0: Sweating helps cool the body, not warm it.
wrongAnswerHints.2: The heart rate does not stop during normal thermoregulation.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Mammals do not change into ectotherms.

questions.text: Which cell structure assembles proteins from amino acids?
questions.explanation: Ribosomes are the sites of protein synthesis, where amino acids are assembled into proteins.

wrongAnswerHints.1: The Golgi apparatus modifies and packages proteins.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Lysosomes break down materials in the cell.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Mitochondria release energy during cellular respiration.

topics: Cell membrane transport and selective permeability

questions.text: Which statement best describes selective permeability of the cell membrane?
options: It allows all substances to enter and leave freely
It allows some substances to cross while blocking others
It only allows water to cross
It prevents any movement across the membrane
questions.explanation: Selective permeability means the membrane controls what enters and leaves the cell.

wrongAnswerHints.0: If everything passed freely, the membrane would not control transport.
wrongAnswerHints.2: Water can cross, but many other substances can also move in or out.
wrongAnswerHints.3: Cells need movement across the membrane to survive.

topics: Human circulatory system and heart anatomy

questions.text: Which structure in the heart receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs before it is pumped to the body?
questions.explanation: The left atrium receives oxygen-rich blood from the lungs through the pulmonary veins and sends it to the left ventricle.

wrongAnswerHints.0: This chamber receives oxygen-poor blood from the body.
wrongAnswerHints.2: This chamber pumps oxygen-poor blood to the lungs.
wrongAnswerHints.3: This chamber pumps oxygen-rich blood out to the body.
